2.text: A game which is called oˊkkal is played with a slender stick and a

3.text: number of small wooden hoops of various sizes (Fig. 197, a). The hoops

4.text: are thrown upwards in a bunch, and one of the party tries to catch on the

5.text: stick as many hoops as possible. The hoops caught are taken off in pairs

6.text: and returned to the general bunch. If there is an odd hoop left over, it is

7.text: said to be “killed.” It is left out of the lot thrown up, and counts one for

8.text: the lucky catcher. This odd hoop also gives him the right to try again. If

9.text: no hoop, or an even number of hoops, is caught, the turn is forfeited, and
